PAPERS.short: Wen landscape fire PM2.5 renal hospitalisations six-country time-series 2026
PAPERS.title: Landscape Fire-Sourced PM2.5 and Cause-Specific Renal Hospitalizations: A Multicountry Two-Stage Time-Series Analysis of 12.5 Million Admissions
PAPERS.pm: Landscape-fire-sourced vs non-fire PM2.5 (per 10 ug/m3, lag 0-5)
PAPERS.geo: Multi-country (Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, New Zealand, Thailand)
PAPERS.n: 12.5 million renal admissions across 1020 locations in six countries, 2000-2019; two-stage time-series with fire-sourced PM2.5 separated from the non-fire remainder. Per 10 ug/m3 cumulative lag 0-5, RR 1.011 (1.007-1.015) for all renal admissions, strongest for acute kidney injury; associations larger for fire-sourced than non-fire PM2.5, larger in warmer areas and graded by GDP per capita. Attributable burden 1.38 admissions per 100,000 per year. Limitation: the fire/non-fire split comes from a chemical-transport-plus-ML partition, not measured tracers, so 'fire PM is more toxic' partly inherits the partition's error structure; heat co-occurs with smoke and dehydration drives AKI, and residual confounding by temperature is the obvious threat. Relevance: moderate - smoke-episode exposure is where LCS density most improves over sparse FRM/FEM coverage.

PAPERS.short: Huang PM2.5 coronary artery dilatation Kawasaki disease case-crossover 2026
PAPERS.title: Association between PM(2.5) and coronary artery dilatation with Kawasaki disease in China
PAPERS.endpoint: Coronary artery dilatation (Z score) in Kawasaki disease
PAPERS.n: 847 children with Kawasaki disease, 2017-2021; case-crossover with a distributed-lag Poisson GLM on coronary Z score. Risk of coronary artery dilatation rose at lags 2-4, peaking at lag 3 with RR 1.11 (1.02-1.21); the abstract does not state the PM2.5 increment. Mediation via CRP, ALT and haemoglobin. Limitation: a case-crossover needs an acute event with a datable onset, yet CAD is detected at echocardiography whose timing follows admission and IVIG, so the referent-window logic is shaky; the 'mediators' are markers of disease severity measured after onset, and the highlights' claim of a 'population-based cohort' contradicts the design. Relevance: low - city-monitor assignment, no sensing implication.

PAPERS.short: Wongcharoen short-term PM2.5 MACE high-risk population nationwide case-crossover 2026
PAPERS.title: Associations between short-term PM(2.5) exposure and major cardiovascular events in high-risk population: a nationwide case-crossover study
PAPERS.geo: Thailand (inferred from author group; not stated in record)
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Wongcharoen et al.); no abstract indexed at harvest. A nationwide time-stratified case-crossover of short-term PM2.5 and major adverse cardiovascular events restricted to a 'high-risk population' (presumably prior CVD, diabetes or hypertension). Country, n, lag structure and effect size cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; case-crossover in a pre-selected high-risk group estimates a conditional acute effect that is not comparable with general-population estimates. Relevance: low-moderate - short-lag acute effects are what real-time LCS alerts are meant to act on.

PAPERS.short: Morales El Paso port-of-entry PM2.5 immigration COPD census tracts 2026
PAPERS.title: Breathing at the Border: PM2.5 Exposure, Immigration, and COPD Across Census Tracts Close to Ports-of-Entry
PAPERS.n: El Paso census tracts; NASA satellite-derived PM2.5 merged with CDC tract COPD prevalence and ACS social vulnerability; GLMs with distance to the port-of-entry. PM2.5 and percent foreign-born non-citizens were positively associated with COPD prevalence; tracts within three miles of a port had higher prevalence, and the PM2.5 effect was stratified by proximity. No coefficients or CIs in the abstract. Limitation: CDC PLACES prevalence is itself small-area modelled from BRFSS demographics, so regressing it on demographic covariates is partly circular; smoking is not addressed; satellite PM2.5 at ~1 km cannot resolve truck-idling gradients at bridge queues. Relevance: high - port-of-entry diesel queues are a textbook case for dense LCS siting.

PAPERS.short: Makacha PRECISE personal ambient PM2.5 monitoring framework pregnancy SSA 2026
PAPERS.title: An integrated climate-structured personal and ambient air pollution monitoring framework embedded within a pregnancy and postpartum cohort in Sub-Saharan Africa
PAPERS.pm: Minute-resolved personal and fixed-site PM2.5 (wearable LCS)
PAPERS.n: PRECISE cohort: 343 pregnant or postpartum women (Gambia 160, Kenya 105, Mozambique 78), two 5-day wearable deployments in opposing seasons recording PM2.5, T, RH and GPS/accelerometry; six fixed health-facility monitors. Calibration by repeated pre-deployment co-location with reference instruments and in-country Deming-regression harmonisation. Yield 3,190 person-days personal and 328 ambient days; inter-sensor R2 >0.72 pre-deployment and >0.75 in country; ambient capture >85% in Gambia and Kenya, lower in Mozambique (connectivity). Limitation: inter-sensor R2 is precision, not accuracy - the reference co-location bias and slope, and the RH correction applied, are not in the abstract; 5-day windows in a purposive subsample limit pregnancy-average inference. Relevance: high - a reusable LCS QA protocol for low-resource cohorts.

PAPERS.short: Intra four co-deployed electrostatic PM monitors power plant agreement 2026
PAPERS.title: Multi-point monitoring of PM10, PM2.5, and PM1.0 at a combined-cycle power plant: field agreement between four co-deployed electrostatic monitors
PAPERS.pm: PM10, PM2.5, PM1.0 (corona charging, impaction, Faraday-cup electrometry)
PAPERS.n: Four prototype three-channel electrostatic mass monitors at a combined-cycle plant, Feb-Jun 2020, 92-100% daily recovery; station means PM10 44.9-54.1, PM2.5 24.8-30.8, PM1.0 7.5-11.9 ug/m3. Fixed station differences explained 0.7% of log 24-h PM10 variance but the day-by-station interaction 57.1%; pairwise 95% limits of agreement spanned ratios 0.35-3.26 (PM10) and 0.33-2.83 (PM2.5); single-unit ICC 0.42 for PM10, 0.75 for the four-unit mean. Disagreement did not shrink with averaging. Limitation: preprint; no reference instrument, so agreement says nothing about accuracy; units were not co-located side by side first, so unit drift and real micro-gradients are separated only by inference. Relevance: high - the same argument applies to any LCS network: station contrasts need routine co-location checks.

PAPERS.short: Arif Agra leather footwear facilities indoor PM2.5 CO2 formaldehyde 2026
PAPERS.title: Indoor Air Quality and Thermal Environment Across Three Leather Footwear Facilities in Agra India
PAPERS.pm: Indoor PM2.5/PM10, I/O PM2.5 ratio, CO2, formaldehyde, TVOC
PAPERS.n: Three leather-footwear facilities (cottage, small, organised), 27 months, 608 sessions. Facility dominated variance for every parameter (partial eta2 0.10-0.87); cottage vs organised means PM2.5 2.0-fold, CO2 1.9-, formaldehyde 3.0- and VOC 3.5-fold higher. Season dominated PM and thermal variables, tracking ventilation; indoor/outdoor PM2.5 ratios 0.48-1.00 across facilities; CO2 above the ASHRAE threshold in 99.5% of cottage sessions vs 0% organised. Limitation: preprint; one facility per tier, so scale is confounded with building; instruments and their calibration are not stated, and spot sessions are not shift-weighted personal exposure. Relevance: moderate - informal-sector workplaces are where portable LCS are the only feasible monitor.

PAPERS.short: Li runway visual range model brown carbon aerosol chromatic effects 2026
PAPERS.title: Refined runway visual range measurement model incorporating brown carbon aerosol effects
PAPERS.n: Optics Letter: conventional runway visual range (RVR) algorithms treat black carbon and scattering aerosol only; brown carbon's wavelength-selective absorption introduces two systematic errors - extinction spectral mismatch between the transmissometer/forward-scatter wavelength and the photopic band, and a chromatic shift in the visual threshold. A refined RVR model including BrC chromatic effects is proposed and 'experimentally validated'. Limitation: no error magnitudes, BrC loadings or validation data in the abstract. Relevance: moderate - the same single-wavelength assumption underlies optical PM sensors, whose mass conversion is biased by absorbing, spectrally selective aerosol.

PAPERS.short: Wu ProNet physics-AI coupled CTM PM2.5 O3 forecasting 338 cities 2026
PAPERS.title: Fusing physics and AI enhances accuracy and diagnostic capabilities in air quality forecasting
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 and O3 forecasts (338 Chinese cities)
PAPERS.n: ProNet embeds observation-constrained neural correctors inside the governing equations of a chemical transport model rather than post-processing its output. On 2022-23 data across 338 Chinese cities it beat the physical CTM and AI-only baselines, generalised better to extreme events outside training, and surpassed forecaster-adjusted operational forecasts by 6.1% (PM2.5) and 3.0% (O3). The correctors yield process-level error bookkeeping that exposes systematic CTM parameterisation biases. Limitation: '6.1% accuracy' is an unspecified metric; one two-year period invites temporal leakage, and process attribution from learned correctors is not unique - compensating errors can be assigned to the wrong process. Relevance: high - in-equation assimilation is the natural slot for dense calibrated LCS observations.

PAPERS.short: Nolles IGP vs NCP PM2.5 pollution forming efficiency CAMS 2026
PAPERS.title: Indo-Gangetic Plain experiences higher aerosol pollution than North China Plain despite lower emissions
PAPERS.pm: CAMS EAC4 PM2.5 vs CAMS-GLOB-ANT emissions
PAPERS.geo: South Asia and China (IGP vs NCP)
PAPERS.n: CAMS EAC4 reanalysis, CAMS-GLOB-ANT emissions and ERA5 for 2019. The NCP emitted 65% more primary PM and precursors (28,860 vs 17,464 kt) yet the IGP had higher annual PM2.5 (123.6 vs 113.2 ug/m3); NCP logged more bad-air days (251 vs 238) but the IGP longer episodes, up to 170 consecutive days around Delhi. A 'pollution forming efficiency' was nearly double in the IGP in winter, attributed to winds <6 km/h and PBL <300 m. Limitation: both concentration and emissions are model products for one year; EAC4 assimilates AOD and is biased in the IGP, and emission inventories under-count agricultural and residential burning there, which inflates the efficiency ratio. Relevance: moderate - quantifies what reanalysis cannot replace ground networks for.

PAPERS.short: Falcon-Gracia BiSC placental sncRNA air pollution maternal smoking 2026
PAPERS.title: Impact of air pollution and tobacco smoke on the placental small non-coding RNA landscape
PAPERS.pm: Prenatal PM2.5, black carbon, NO2 (hybrid dispersion-LUR)
PAPERS.n: 390 chorionic villus samples from the Barcelona Life Study Cohort, small-RNA sequencing; 979 sncRNA clusters (miRNA 33%, piRNA 26%, snoRNA 12%, tRF 8%). Maternal smoking was associated with miR-421 down-regulation and up-regulation of SNORD113/114 snoRNAs at the imprinted DLK1-DIO3 locus and piR-26394. No sncRNA was associated with PM2.5, BC or NO2 after multiple-testing correction; several miRNAs were suggestive. Limitation: preprint; a null after FDR across ~1000 features at n=390 says little about effect absence, and pregnancy-average LUR exposure is a blunt contrast for trimester-specific placental biology. Relevance: low - a usefully reported null for PM against a positive smoking control.

PAPERS.short: Kim pig building air cleaner TSP PM2.5 productivity 2026
PAPERS.title: Association between indoor air pollutants and pig productivity index by on-site application of air cleaner
PAPERS.pm: TSP, PM2.5, airborne fungi in pig housing
PAPERS.endpoint: Pig weight gain, feed conversion, activity, mortality
PAPERS.n: One commercial pig building, control vs air-cleaner-treated room, monitored six months across rearing stages. Air-cleaner reduction efficiency rose with stage, 5-10% at farrowing to 30-45% at fattening; treated rooms showed better weight gain, feed conversion, activity index and mortality. Weight gain and activity correlated with TSP and PM2.5 (and airborne fungi). Limitation: one room per arm, no randomisation or replication - room effects are inseparable from treatment; the cleaner technology and PM instrumentation are not stated. Relevance: low - livestock housing is a large agricultural PM source and an occupational exposure for farm workers, but this design supports neither inference.

PAPERS.short: Kirsanov COSMO-ART Saint Petersburg UHI pollution PM10 feedback 2026
PAPERS.title: Assessing Urban Pollution and Heat Island Feedback in a Northern Megacity Using the Fully Coupled COSMO-ART Model
PAPERS.pm: Near-surface PM10, NO, CO, O3; aerosol radiative feedback
PAPERS.n: COSMO-ART with TERRA_URB for winter and summer episodes in Saint Petersburg. UHI-driven mixing and deeper PBL cut near-surface primary pollutants 15-54% (winter) and 5-33% (summer), PM10 peaks by >44%, while O3 rose. Aerosol radiative feedback on the UHI was weak (hundredths of a degree, peaks <0.3 C), cooling in summer and warming over winter snow, under a fifth of canopy forcing. Limitation: two episodes, model-only; no comparison with observed PM10 is reported in the abstract, and PM10 in a snowy city is dominated by road-dust resuspension that emission inventories handle poorly. Relevance: moderate - urban/rural LCS gradients conflate emission density with UHI-enhanced dilution.

PAPERS.short: Imran Chinese cities urban air quality determinants interpretable ML 2014-2023
PAPERS.title: Spatio-temporal variation and determinants of urban air quality in Chinese cities during 2014-2023: an interpretable machine learning analysis
PAPERS.pm: City-level air quality (PM2.5 presumably among pollutants)
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only; no abstract retrievable at harvest. The title describes a decade (2014-2023) of spatio-temporal variation in Chinese urban air quality with interpretable ML (SHAP-type attribution) of its determinants. Pollutants, number of cities, predictors and model skill cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; SHAP attributions on correlated socio-economic and meteorological predictors are not causal, and the 2014-2023 decline is dominated by the 2013 and 2018 action plans. Relevance: low - monitor-network secondary analysis.

PAPERS.short: Prieto Perez Huszar future central European air quality emission changes 2026
PAPERS.title: The role that changes in emissions play in future central European air-quality
PAPERS.pm: Future PM and O3 under emission scenarios (presumably)
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Prieto Perez, Huszar, Karlicky); no abstract retrievable at harvest. The group runs regional climate-chemistry (RegCM/WRF-CAMx) scenarios; the title separates the emission-change contribution to future central European air quality from climate change. Pollutants, scenarios and horizons cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; scenario attribution depends on the emission pathway chosen. Relevance: low - policy context for the PM levels European LCS networks will measure.

PAPERS.short: Li atmospheric cadmium concentration deposition China modelling 2026
PAPERS.title: Modeling the spatial distributions and seasonal variations of atmospheric cadmium concentration and deposition in China
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only; no abstract retrievable at harvest. National modelling of atmospheric cadmium - carried almost entirely on fine particles - with its spatial and seasonal distribution and deposition. Model, inventory, resolution and evaluation against measured Cd cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; metal inventories for smelting and coal are the dominant uncertainty. Relevance: low - mass-only LCS cannot see toxic trace-metal fractions, which is why such composition models remain needed.

PAPERS.short: Liu Beijing autumn-winter PM2.5 oxidative potential source predictors 2026
PAPERS.title: Autumn-winter variability and source-related predictors of PM2.5 oxidative potential in urban Beijing
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 oxidative potential (assay not stated) and source tracers
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only; no abstract retrievable at harvest. An autumn-winter campaign relating PM2.5 oxidative potential in urban Beijing to source-related predictors (heating, traffic, secondary formation presumably). Assay (DTT, AA, GSH), sample count and predictive model cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; a single season and site. Relevance: high - follows the 19 Oct Guangdong OP finding; if OP is predictable from source tracers, a subset of networked sensors with composition proxies could map it.

PAPERS.short: Sharma Singapore aerosol type classification ground remote sensing reanalysis 2026
PAPERS.title: Aerosol Types Classification in the Tropical Climate of Singapore by Integrating Ground-Based Remote Sensing and Reanalysis Datasets
PAPERS.pm: Columnar aerosol optical properties (AOD, Angstrom exponent presumably)
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only; no abstract retrievable at harvest. Aerosol-type classification in tropical Singapore combining ground-based remote sensing (AERONET sun photometer presumably) with reanalysis (MERRA-2/CAMS). Classification scheme, period and the share of transboundary smoke cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; columnar typing does not map one-to-one onto surface PM. Relevance: moderate - aerosol type drives optical-LCS response (hygroscopicity, refractive index) and so the calibration regime a tropical network needs.

PAPERS.short: Kheder Foehn generative km-scale global PM2.5 forecast 2026
PAPERS.title: Global probabilistic forecasting of air pollution
PAPERS.pm: Global kilometre-scale PM2.5 estimates (training and target)
PAPERS.n: Foehn, a generative model trained on global kilometre-scale PM2.5 estimates that also computes air-mass origin. In one year of retrospective forecasts it beat the operational forecast at three of four stations; its ensembles are reported as calibrated, and the ensemble mean detects local pollution extremes four days ahead about as well as the operational system does one day ahead. Limitation: preprint; 'kilometre-scale estimates' are themselves satellite/model fusion products, so skill is partly measured against the training distribution, and the authors concede real-time km-scale inputs do not yet exist - operational use is hypothetical. Skill metrics and station counts are not given in the abstract. Relevance: high - calibrated LCS networks are the plausible real-time km-scale input this model says it lacks.
